record.paper_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
record.original_question: What is the correct solution of color confinement in QCD, beyond the existing lattice result for the large-distance potential between two static quarks, where the potential approaches sigma r + const/r as the separation r goes to infinity?

evidence.quote: The most challenging QCD problem –confinement– is not yet solved, in spite of a one M$ prize awaiting whoever solves it.137
Almost all we have concerning confinement is the good old “stringy” lattice result for the potential V (r) between two static quarks, V (r) → σ r + const/r, as r → ∞, with σ the string’s tension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-abelian gauge theory with gauge group SU(3) coupled to quark fields in the fundamental representation, defined (formally) by the Yang-Mills Lagrangian with quarks. Numerical lattice gauge theory computations indicate that the static potential V(r) between an infinitely heavy quark-antiquark pair separated by a distance r satisfies, at large r, the asymptotic behavior

   V(r) ~ sigma * r + c/r   as r -> infinity,

where sigma > 0 is the string tension and c is a constant (the so-called Lüscher term). This linear rise is the conventional indicator of color confinement: isolated colored states do not appear in the physical spectrum.

Problem. Provide a mathematically rigorous derivation, from first principles of the (continuum) SU(3) Yang-Mills theory with quarks, of color confinement. Concretely:

(a) Construct the quantum SU(3) Yang-Mills theory on R^4 (in a Wightman/Osterwalder-Schrader or equivalent rigorous sense) and prove that it has a positive mass gap.

(b) Prove that the physical Hilbert space contains no asymptotic states transforming nontrivially under the global color SU(3): all finite-energy states are color singlets.

(c) Prove the area law for large Wilson loops in the pure gauge theory, equivalently establish that the static quark-antiquark potential V(r) is confining, and in particular satisfies V(r) -> infinity as r -> infinity (ideally with linear leading behavior V(r) ~ sigma r with sigma > 0).

Give a complete mathematical proof, or otherwise determine the correct mechanism and analytic description of confinement in QCD.
artifact.status_search_result: Color confinement and the existence of a mass gap in Yang-Mills theory remain a famous open problem; it is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems and, as of 2026, no rigorous solution has been accepted. Only nonperturbative lattice and model-based evidence is available.

status_evidence.title: Yang-Mills and Mass Gap — Clay Mathematics Institute
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap. This problem is unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: The Yang-Mills mass gap / confinement problem is listed as an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem.

status_evidence.title: Color confinement - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There is not yet an analytic proof of color confinement in any non-abelian gauge theory.
status_evidence.claim: No analytic proof of color confinement is currently known.
